source.text: שִׁמְע֞וּ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה פָּר֤וֹת הַבָּשָׁן֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן הָעֹשְׁק֣וֹת דַּלִּ֔ים הָרֹצְצ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים הָאֹמְרֹ֥ת לַאֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֖ם הָבִ֥יאָה וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear this word, cows of the Bashan who [are] on [the] mountain of Samaria, who oppress [the] poor, who crush [the] needy, who say to their lords: Bring, and let us drink.

en.L: Hear this word, cows of Bashan, you who [are] on the mount of Samaria, \q you who oppress the poor, \q who crush the needy, \q who say to their lords, "Bring, and let us drink!"
en.B: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the hill of Samaria, \q you who oppress the poor \q and crush the needy, \q who say to their husbands, "Bring us something to drink!"
en.R: Listen to this message, you women of Samaria, as fat as the cows of Bashan. \q You mistreat poor people \q and crush those in need. \q You say to your husbands, "Bring us more to drink!"

pt.L: Ouçam esta palavra, vacas de Basã, vocês que [estão] no monte de Samaria, \q vocês que oprimem os pobres, \q que esmagam os necessitados, \q que dizem aos seus senhores: "Tragam, e bebamos!"
pt.B: Ouçam esta palavra, vacas de Basã, vocês que estão no monte de Samaria, \q que oprimem os pobres \q e esmagam os necessitados, \q que dizem aos seus maridos: "Tragam bebida para nós!"
pt.R: Escutem esta mensagem, mulheres de Samaria, gordas como as vacas de Basã! \q Vocês maltratam os pobres \q e esmagam os necessitados. \q Vocês dizem aos seus maridos: "Tragam mais bebida para nós!"

decisions.choice: cows of Bashan: the sleek, well-fed cattle of the richest grazing land
decisions.reason: Bashan was the high plateau east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its rich pasture and its strong, well-fed cattle (Deuteronomy 32:14; Psalm 22:13; Ezekiel 39:18). To call people "cows of Bashan" pictures them as pampered and fat on the best of everything, while they live off the poor. Verses 2-3 show where such cattle end up: led away through the breaches.

decisions.choice: the cows are the wealthy women of Samaria
alternatives: the rich rulers of Samaria, men and women
decisions.reason: The participles "who oppress", "who crush" and "who say" are feminine, and in verse 3 "each woman" goes out through the breaches. They speak to "their lords", their husbands. So the words are addressed to the rich women of the capital. Some pronouns in verses 1-3 are masculine ("their lords", "upon you" in verse 2), a mixing found elsewhere in Hebrew, and some take the "cows" more widely, as the rich and powerful of Samaria, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: their lords: their husbands
decisions.reason: A wife could call her husband "my lord" (Genesis 18:12; Judges 19:26-27). The word also hints at the irony: the women give the orders, and their "lords" obey.

decisions.choice: oppress the poor ... "Bring, and let us drink!": their drinking is paid for by the poor
decisions.reason: The women may not oppress the poor with their own hands, but their demands for wine drive their husbands to squeeze the poor for it. The same pair, "the poor" and "the needy", stands in 2:6-7 and 8:4-6.

decisions.choice: you women of Samaria, as fat as the cows of Bashan (R); husbands (B, R); lords (L)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "cows" are and what the picture means, following m2. Since m2 is uncertain, so is this wording. Balanced and Readable say "husbands" for "lords" (m3); Readable says "your husbands" because it speaks to the women directly throughout.

decisions.choice: as vacas de Basã (L, B); mulheres de Samaria, gordas como as vacas de Basã (R)
decisions.reason: "Vacas de Basã" keeps the picture (m1); the Portuguese feminine "vacas" already fits the women addressed (m2). Readable says who they are, as the English does, and like it is only as certain as m2. They are addressed as "vocês", a group of people.

decisions.choice: os seus senhores (L); os seus maridos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "senhores"; Balanced and Readable say "maridos" (m3), as the English does.

source.text: נִשְׁבַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּקָדְשׁ֔וֹ כִּ֛י הִנֵּ֥ה יָמִ֖ים בָּאִ֣ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְנִשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ בְּצִנּ֔וֹת וְאַחֲרִיתְכֶ֖ן בְּסִיר֥וֹת דּוּגָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has sworn [the] Lord Yahweh by his holiness: For look, days [are] coming upon you, and one will lift you away with hooks, and your remnant with fishhooks.

en.L: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: \q Look, days are coming upon you \q when they will carry you away with hooks, \q and the last of you with fishhooks.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: \q The time is surely coming for you \q when you will be dragged away with hooks, \q the last of you with fishhooks.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has made a solemn promise by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own holiness: \q The time is coming for you \q when your enemies will drag you away with hooks, \q every last one of you, like fish on hooks.

pt.L: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} jurou pela {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santidade: \q Eis que vêm dias sobre vocês \q em que as levarão com ganchos, \q e o resto de vocês com anzóis.
pt.B: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} jurou pela {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} santidade: \q Certamente vem o tempo para vocês \q em que serão arrastadas com ganchos, \q e as últimas de vocês, com anzóis.
pt.R: O Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} fez um juramento solene pela {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} própria santidade: \q Está chegando o tempo para vocês \q em que os seus inimigos vão arrastar vocês com ganchos, \q cada uma de vocês, como peixes presos em anzóis.

decisions.choice: sworn by his holiness: the LORD swears by what he is, so the oath cannot fail
decisions.reason: People swear by something greater than themselves; the LORD can swear only by himself (6:8), by his holiness (Psalm 89:36), or by what he has made his own (8:7). His holiness stands against the profaning of his name (2:7). It is the surest of oaths.

decisions.choice: days are coming: the time is coming
decisions.reason: The phrase announces a coming time of judgment or of restoration (8:11; 9:13; Jeremiah 7:32).

decisions.choice: hooks ... fishhooks: the captives are dragged away like fish on hooks
alternatives: carried away in baskets, the last of you in fish pots
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. They are usually taken as hooks or barbs, the second as fishing hooks, and conquerors are pictured leading captives with hooks (2 Kings 19:28; Ezekiel 19:4; 29:4). The words can also mean thorns and pots, so that the people are carried off in baskets as fish were. "The last of you" may also be "your descendants". On every reading, the cows of Bashan are taken away like animals or fish.

decisions.choice: they will carry you away: the enemy, not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject ("one will lift you away"), as Hebrew does when the doer does not matter. It is the enemy of 3:11.

decisions.choice: The time is surely coming (B); has made a solemn promise; your enemies; like fish on hooks (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "days are coming" (m2). Readable explains the oath and names the enemy as the doer (m4).

decisions.choice: Eis que vêm dias (L); Certamente vem o tempo (B); Está chegando o tempo (R); feminine forms
decisions.reason: "Eis que vêm dias" is the prophets' formula at Literal, as Isaiah and Jeremiah have it in Portuguese; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m2). The words are still spoken to the women of verse 1, so Portuguese uses feminine forms ("as levarão", "arrastadas", "as últimas", "cada uma").

source.text: וּפְרָצִ֥ים תֵּצֶ֖אנָה אִשָּׁ֣ה נֶגְדָּ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּ֥נָה הַהַרְמ֖וֹנָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And through breaches you will go out, each woman before her, and you will be cast toward the Harmon, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And through the breaches you will go out, each [woman] straight ahead, \q and you will be cast out toward Harmon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You will go out through the breaches in the wall, each one straight ahead, \q and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You will go out through the holes in the broken walls, each of you straight ahead, \q and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E pelas brechas sairão, cada uma em frente, \q e serão lançadas para Harmom, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Vocês sairão pelas brechas do muro, cada uma em frente, \q e serão lançadas para Harmom, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Vocês vão sair pelos buracos dos muros derrubados, uma atrás da outra, \q e vão ser jogadas para os lados de Harmom, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: through the breaches ... each straight ahead: led out through the gaps in the broken walls, one behind another
decisions.reason: When a city fell, its walls were breached and its people led out through the gaps. "Each straight ahead" pictures them going in file, unable to turn aside, like cattle driven through a broken fence (compare Joshua 6:5, 20).

decisions.choice: you will be cast out: reading the verb as passive
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels give an active verb, "you will cast out", with no object, which is hard to make sense of. The same letters read with other vowels give "you will be cast out", and several ancient translations take it that way. That reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: Harmon: a place not otherwise known
decisions.reason: Harmon is named nowhere else, and its location is unknown. Some take it as Mount Hermon in the far north, on the road to exile, or read it with the ancient translations as another name; it may also be a word for a place of refuse. It is clearly the place where the captives are thrown.

decisions.choice: in the wall (B), in the broken walls (R); each one (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the breaches are (m1). Literal brackets "woman", which the Hebrew gives in a feminine word for "each".

decisions.choice: cada uma (L, B), uma atrás da outra (R); Harmom
decisions.reason: Portuguese "cada uma" carries the feminine the Hebrew has, so Literal needs no bracket. The unknown place (m3) is spelled "Harmom", not identified with Mount Hermon ("Hermom").

source.text: בֹּ֤אוּ בֵֽית־אֵל֙ וּפִשְׁע֔וּ הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל הַרְבּ֣וּ לִפְשֹׁ֑עַ וְהָבִ֤יאוּ לַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ זִבְחֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים מַעְשְׂרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Come to Bethel and transgress; to the Gilgal, multiply to transgress; and bring to the morning your sacrifices, to three days your tithes.

en.L: Come to Bethel and transgress; \q to Gilgal, and multiply transgressing; \q and bring your sacrifices every morning, \q your tithes every three days;
en.B: Go to Bethel and rebel! \q Go to Gilgal and rebel even more! \q Bring your sacrifices every morning, \q your tithes every three days!
en.R: Go ahead! Go to Bethel and sin! \q Go to Gilgal and sin even more! \q Bring your sacrifices every morning \q and your tithes every three days!

pt.L: Venham a Betel e transgridam; \q a Gilgal, multipliquem as transgressões; \q e tragam pela manhã os seus sacrifícios, \q a cada três dias os seus dízimos;
pt.B: Vão a Betel e rebelem-se! \q Vão a Gilgal e rebelem-se ainda mais! \q Tragam os seus sacrifícios todas as manhãs \q e os seus dízimos a cada três dias!
pt.R: Vamos! Vão a Betel e pequem! \q Vão a Gilgal e pequem ainda mais! \q Tragam os seus sacrifícios todas as manhãs \q e os seus dízimos a cada três dias!

decisions.choice: Come to Bethel and transgress: a priest's call to worship, turned upside down
decisions.reason: A priest would call pilgrims to "come" to the shrine and worship. Amos uses the same words to say "come and transgress": their worship itself is rebellion against the LORD, because they offer it while oppressing the poor (5:4-5, 21-24).

decisions.choice: Bethel and Gilgal: the main shrines of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Bethel was the royal shrine (3:14; 7:13). Gilgal, near Jericho, was where Israel first camped in the land and where Saul was made king (Joshua 4:19-20; 1 Samuel 11:15). Both were busy places of pilgrimage, condemned also by Hosea (Hosea 4:15; 9:15) and in Amos 5:5.

decisions.choice: every morning ... every three days: worship carried far beyond what the law asked
alternatives: on the morning (after you arrive) ... on the third day
decisions.reason: Tithes were brought once a year, and every third year for the poor (Deuteronomy 14:22-29), and sacrifices at the feasts. Bringing sacrifices daily and tithes every three days is sarcasm: the more zealous their worship, the more they sin. Some read the phrases as "in the morning" and "on the third day" of a pilgrimage, the days on which offerings were brought after arrival.

decisions.choice: transgress (L), rebel (B), sin (R)
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with the noun "transgression" of the refrain of chapters 1-2. It follows Amos's settled wording for the noun: "transgression" (Literal), "crime / rebellion" (Balanced) and "sin" (Readable). Balanced says "rebel" because here the wrong is done against God. Balanced and Readable repeat "Go" in the second line, which the Hebrew leaves implied; Readable adds "Go ahead!" to mark the sarcasm.

decisions.choice: transgridam (L), rebelem-se (B), pequem (R)
decisions.reason: The verb of the noun in the refrain (1:3) follows the English levels; Balanced says "rebelem-se", the sense of the root (m1), since "transgredir" as a command reads stiffly. Betel and Gilgal take their usual Portuguese forms.

source.text: וְקַטֵּ֤ר מֵֽחָמֵץ֙ תּוֹדָ֔ה וְקִרְא֥וּ נְדָב֖וֹת הַשְׁמִ֑יעוּ כִּ֣י כֵ֤ן אֲהַבְתֶּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And burn from leavened [bread] a thank offering, and proclaim freewill offerings, make [them] heard; for so you love, sons of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: and burn a thank offering of leavened bread, \q and proclaim freewill offerings, make [them] heard; \q for so you love [to do], {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Burn a thank offering of leavened bread, \q and announce your freewill offerings, make them known! \q For this is what you love to do, {{gender:people|sons}} of Israel, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Burn bread made with yeast as a thank offering. \q Tell everyone about the gifts you bring freely, and make sure they hear! \q People of Israel, this is the kind of thing you love to do, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: e queimem pão fermentado como sacrifício de ação de graças, \q e proclamem ofertas voluntárias, façam[-nas] ouvir; \q pois assim vocês amam [fazer], filhos de Israel, \q declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.B: Queimem pão com fermento como sacrifício de ação de graças, \q e anunciem as suas ofertas voluntárias, façam que todos saibam! \q Pois é isso que vocês amam fazer, israelitas, \q declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.R: Queimem pão feito com fermento como oferta de agradecimento. \q Contem para todo mundo as ofertas que vocês dão por vontade própria, e façam questão de que todos ouçam! \q Povo de Israel, é desse tipo de coisa que vocês gostam, \q diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: burn a thank offering of leavened bread: an offering made in a way the law did not allow
decisions.reason: Nothing with leaven (yeast) was to be burned on the altar (Leviticus 2:11). With a thank offering, loaves of leavened bread were brought to be eaten, not burned (Leviticus 7:13). Burning it may show that their worship pleases themselves rather than keeping to what the LORD asked.

decisions.choice: proclaim freewill offerings, make them heard: showing off gifts that should be given freely
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was a gift beyond what was required (Leviticus 7:16; 22:18). They announce theirs publicly, so that everyone knows how generous they are.

decisions.choice: for so you love: this is the religion you enjoy
decisions.reason: The point of the sarcasm: they love their worship, but it is worship that suits them, not the LORD (5:21-23).

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B), says the Lord GOD (R); children (sons) of Israel (L), people (sons) of Israel (B), People of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula follows Ezekiel's table: "declares the Lord GOD" at Literal and Balanced and "says the Lord GOD" at Readable. Literal begins with "and", since the Hebrew sentence runs on from verse 4.

decisions.choice: sacrifício de ação de graças; ofertas voluntárias; filhos de Israel (L), israelitas (B), no gender setting
decisions.reason: The offerings take the words Leviticus 7:12-16 gives them in Portuguese (m1, m2). As at 2:11, "filhos" and "israelitas" already include women, so the English gender span has no second Portuguese wording.

source.text: וְגַם־אֲנִי֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם נִקְי֤וֹן שִׁנַּ֨יִם֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם וְחֹ֣סֶר לֶ֔חֶם בְּכֹ֖ל מְקוֹמֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also I gave to you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, \q and shortage of bread \q in all your places; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I also gave you clean teeth in all your cities \q and lack of bread in all your towns. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I made you go hungry in all your cities. \q There was no food anywhere you lived. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E eu também lhes dei limpeza de dentes em todas as suas cidades, \q e falta de pão \q em todos os seus lugares; \q mas vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Eu também lhes dei dentes limpos em todas as suas cidades \q e falta de pão em todos os seus povoados. \q Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Eu fiz vocês passarem fome em todas as suas cidades. \q Não havia comida em nenhum lugar onde vocês moravam. \q Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: cleanness of teeth: nothing to chew, famine
decisions.reason: Teeth stay clean when there is nothing to eat. The parallel line says it plainly: lack of bread.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: you did not turn back to the LORD; the refrain of verses 6-11
decisions.reason: To "return" to the LORD is to come back to him in repentance and loyalty (Deuteronomy 4:30; Hosea 6:1; 14:2). The Hebrew says "return as far as me", the same words as Hosea 14:2 and Joel 2:12: a coming back all the way to the LORD himself, not a gesture toward him. Each blow in verses 6-11 was meant to bring Israel back, and each ends with the same words. The wording is kept the same in all five, and the notes here apply to all of them.

decisions.choice: famine, drought, blight, locusts, plague, sword and overthrow: the warnings of the covenant
decisions.reason: The blows of verses 6-11 match the curses the covenant warned of if Israel turned away (Leviticus 26:14-39; Deuteronomy 28:15-68), and the disasters Solomon asked the LORD to hear Israel's prayers in (1 Kings 8:33-40). In Leviticus 26 the warnings come in rounds, each one asking whether Israel will now listen. The LORD "gave" famine as they "brought" their sacrifices (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the refrain: yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD (L); Yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD (B); But even then you did not come back to me, says the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: This wording is used unchanged in verses 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. Literal and Balanced keep the key word "return", which is also the word for repenting. Readable says "come back" and adds "even then" to show that the people did not turn back even after each blow. The closing formula follows the settled "declares the LORD" / "says the LORD".

decisions.choice: clean teeth (B); go hungry, no food (R); towns (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of clean teeth, which the parallel line explains; Readable says what it means (m1). "Places" means the places where people lived: their towns.

decisions.choice: mas vocês não voltaram para mim, declara o SENHOR (L); Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para mim, declara o SENHOR (B); Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para mim, diz o SENHOR (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain of verses 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11 keeps one wording at each level. "Voltar para" is the plain verb of coming back, and also of returning to God in repentance (m2), so Readable can keep it where the English says "come back".

source.text: וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִי֩ מָנַ֨עְתִּי מִכֶּ֜ם אֶת־הַגֶּ֗שֶׁם בְּע֨וֹד שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ לַקָּצִ֔יר וְהִמְטַרְתִּי֙ עַל־עִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת וְעַל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֖ת לֹ֣א אַמְטִ֑יר חֶלְקָ֤ה אַחַת֙ תִּמָּטֵ֔ר וְחֶלְקָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־תַמְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also I withheld from you the rain while yet three months to the harvest; and I would send rain on one city, and on another city I would not send rain; one portion would be rained on, and [the] portion on which it did not rain would wither.

en.L: And I also withheld the rain from you while [it was] still three months to the harvest; \q and I would send rain on one city, \q and on another city I would not send rain; \q one field would be rained on, \q and the field on which it did not rain would wither.
en.B: I also held back the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. \q I would send rain on one town \q but no rain on another. \q One field would get rain, \q and the field that got none would dry up.
en.R: I also kept the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. \q I sent rain on one town \q but not on another. \q One field got rain, \q but a field without rain dried up.

pt.L: E eu também retive de vocês a chuva quando ainda [faltavam] três meses para a colheita; \q e eu fazia chover sobre uma cidade, \q e sobre outra cidade não fazia chover; \q um campo recebia chuva, \q e o campo sobre o qual não chovia secava.
pt.B: Também retive a chuva quando ainda faltavam três meses para a colheita. \q Eu fazia chover sobre uma cidade \q e não sobre outra. \q Um campo recebia chuva, \q e o campo que não recebia secava.
pt.R: Eu também não deixei chover quando ainda faltavam três meses para a colheita. \q Mandei chuva para uma cidade \q mas não para outra. \q Um campo recebeu chuva, \q mas o campo sem chuva secou.

decisions.choice: the rain withheld three months before the harvest: the late rains that the grain needed
decisions.reason: In Israel the rains fall from autumn to spring. The last rains, in late winter and spring, swell the grain before the harvest in April and May (Deuteronomy 11:14; Jeremiah 3:3; Joel 2:23). Without them the crop fails.

decisions.choice: rain on one town and not on another: a sign that the drought came from the LORD
decisions.reason: Rain falling on one town and not the next, on one field and not its neighbor, showed that this was no ordinary dry season. The covenant tied the rain to Israel's faithfulness (Deuteronomy 11:13-17; 1 Kings 8:35-36; 17:1). The verbs describe something that happened again and again.

decisions.choice: city (L), town (B, R); portion of ground (L field), field (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used of any walled town, and "town" fits the many small places meant here. The word translated "field" means a portion of land, a plot.

decisions.choice: cidade; campo
decisions.reason: Portuguese "cidade" covers both a city and a small town, so Balanced and Readable keep it where the English says "town"; "campo" is the plain word for a plot of farmland.

source.text: וְנָע֡וּ שְׁתַּיִם֩ שָׁלֹ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים אֶל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֛ת לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֑עוּ וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And staggered two, three cities to one city to drink water, and not they were satisfied; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And two, three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and they were not filled; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: People from two or three towns staggered to another town for water but could not get enough to drink. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People from two or three towns stumbled to another town for water, but there was not enough to drink. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E duas, três cidades cambaleavam até uma cidade para beber água, e não se saciavam; \q mas vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Gente de duas ou três cidades ia cambaleando até outra cidade para beber água, mas não conseguia matar a sede. \q Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Gente de duas ou três cidades ia cambaleando até outra cidade para buscar água, mas não havia o bastante para beber. \q Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: two, three cities: several towns
decisions.reason: "Two, three" means a few, several (compare Isaiah 17:6). The people of several towns went, weak with thirst, to one town that still had water.

decisions.choice: staggered: went unsteadily, weak from thirst
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander or to stagger (Psalm 107:27; Lamentations 4:14-15).

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: People from (B, R); towns (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the towns staggered; Balanced and Readable say that their people did.

source.text: הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶם֮ בַּשִּׁדָּפ֣וֹן וּבַיֵּרָקוֹן֒ הַרְבּ֨וֹת גַּנּוֹתֵיכֶ֧ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֛ם וּתְאֵנֵיכֶ֥ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֖ם יֹאכַ֣ל הַגָּזָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I struck you with blight and with mildew; [the] many of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees, the locust devoured; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I struck you with blight and with mildew; \q the many of your gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees, the cutting locust devoured; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I struck you with blight and mildew; \q the cutting locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and olive groves. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I struck your crops with diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow. \q Locusts ate up your many gardens and vineyards, and your fig trees and olive trees. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Eu feri vocês com crestamento e com míldio; \q a multidão das suas hortas e das suas vinhas, das suas figueiras e das suas oliveiras, o gafanhoto cortador devorou; \q mas vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Eu feri vocês com crestamento e míldio; \q o gafanhoto cortador devorou as suas muitas hortas e vinhas, as suas figueiras e os seus olivais. \q Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Eu castiguei as suas plantações com doenças que as secaram e as deixaram amarelas. \q Os gafanhotos comeram as suas muitas hortas e vinhas, as suas figueiras e as suas oliveiras. \q Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew: grain scorched by the hot wind and yellowed by disease
decisions.reason: The first word means scorching, the withering of grain by the hot east wind (Genesis 41:6); the second means a yellowing, mildew or rust. The two are named together among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:22) and in Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:37).

decisions.choice: Haggai 2:17 repeats these words
decisions.reason: Haggai 2:17 takes up this verse: "I struck you with blight and mildew and hail ... yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD". Haggai applies Amos's words to the people of his own day.

decisions.choice: the many of your gardens: your many gardens
alternatives: I laid waste your gardens and vineyards
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a verb form meaning "making many", used here as "your many gardens". It is awkward, and a small change of letters would give "I laid waste your gardens", which some prefer.

decisions.choice: the cutting locust: one of the names for the locust
decisions.reason: The word is the first of the four names for locusts in Joel 1:4, where they may be kinds or stages of the insect. Here it stands for a swarm that ate everything.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew (L, B), diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow (R); the cutting locust (L, B), Locusts (R)
decisions.reason: "The cutting locust" is the wording used for this word in Joel 1:4; Readable says "locusts", as Readable does there. Readable explains the two crop diseases (m1).

decisions.choice: crestamento e míldio; o gafanhoto cortador
decisions.reason: The two diseases of grain (m1) take the words Deuteronomy 28:22 gives them in Portuguese. Haggai 2:17, which repeats the verse (m2), should keep them. "Gafanhoto cortador" names the first locust of Joel 1:4, as the English does.

source.text: שִׁלַּ֨חְתִּי בָכֶ֥ם דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם הָרַ֤גְתִּי בַחֶ֨רֶב֙ בַּח֣וּרֵיכֶ֔ם עִ֖ם שְׁבִ֣י סֽוּסֵיכֶ֑ם וָאַעֲלֶ֞ה בְּאֹ֤שׁ מַחֲנֵיכֶם֙ וּֽבְאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I sent among you pestilence after [the] manner of Egypt; I killed with the sword your young men, along with [the] capture of your horses, and I made go up [the] stench of your camps even into your nostrils; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I sent pestilence among you in the manner of Egypt; \q I killed with the sword your young men, \q along with your captured horses; \q and I made the stench of your camps rise even into your nostrils; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I sent a plague among you as I did on Egypt; \q I killed your young men with the sword, \q and your horses were captured; \q I made the stench of your camps fill your nostrils. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I sent diseases among you like the ones I sent on Egypt. \q I killed your young men in battle, \q and your horses were taken away. \q I made you smell the stink of dead bodies in your camps. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Enviei entre vocês a peste à maneira do Egito; \q matei à espada os seus jovens, \q junto com os seus cavalos capturados; \q e fiz subir o mau cheiro dos seus acampamentos até as suas narinas; \q mas vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Mandei uma epidemia entre vocês, como fiz com o Egito; \q matei à espada os seus jovens, \q e os seus cavalos foram capturados; \q fiz o mau cheiro dos seus acampamentos encher as suas narinas. \q Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Mandei para vocês doenças como as que mandei para o Egito. \q Matei os seus jovens na guerra, \q e os seus cavalos foram levados. \q Fiz vocês sentirem o fedor dos cadáveres nos seus acampamentos. \q Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: pestilence in the manner of Egypt: the plagues the LORD once sent on Egypt now strike Israel
decisions.reason: The LORD struck Egypt with pestilence (Exodus 9:3, 15), and the covenant warned that Israel would suffer "the diseases of Egypt" if it turned away (Deuteronomy 28:27, 60). "In the manner of" may also be read "on the road to" Egypt, but the link with the exodus plagues fits the verse best.

decisions.choice: young men killed, horses captured: defeat in war
decisions.reason: Israel's young men died in battle and its horses, the strength of its chariot force, were taken. In the wars with Aram Israel was left with only fifty horsemen and ten chariots (2 Kings 13:7).

decisions.choice: the stench of your camps: the smell of the unburied dead
decisions.reason: After defeat, the dead lay unburied in the army's camp, and the stench rose (Isaiah 34:3; Joel 2:20).

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: pestilence (L), plague (B), diseases (R); in battle (R); dead bodies (R)
decisions.reason: "Pestilence", "plague" and "disease" are the settled wording for this word. Readable says "in battle" for "with the sword" and says what made the stench (m3).

decisions.choice: a peste (L); uma epidemia (B); doenças (R)
decisions.reason: The word follows the English levels; "praga" is avoided at Balanced because Brazilian readers hear in it a curse or a plague of insects rather than a disease.

source.text: הָפַ֣כְתִּי בָכֶ֗ם כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֤ת אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־סְדֹ֣ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה וַתִּהְי֕וּ כְּא֖וּד מֻצָּ֣ל מִשְׂרֵפָ֑הוְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I overthrew among you as [the] overthrow of God [of] Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a firebrand snatched from [the] burning; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I overthrew [some] among you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, \q and you were like a stick snatched from the burning; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I overthrew some of you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, \q and you became like a burning stick pulled out of the fire. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I destroyed some of you as completely as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. \q The rest of you were like a burning stick pulled out of a fire just in time. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: Eu destruí [alguns] entre vocês, como Deus destruiu Sodoma e Gomorra, \q e vocês ficaram como um tição tirado do fogo; \q mas vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Destruí alguns de vocês como Deus destruiu Sodoma e Gomorra, \q e vocês ficaram como um tição arrancado do fogo. \q Mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Destruí alguns de vocês tão completamente como Deus destruiu Sodoma e Gomorra. \q Os outros ficaram como um pedaço de pau em brasa tirado do fogo bem na hora. \q Mas mesmo assim vocês não voltaram para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah: utter destruction
decisions.reason: The overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25) became the standard picture of total ruin (Deuteronomy 29:22; Isaiah 1:9; 13:19; Jeremiah 49:18). The LORD speaks of himself as "God" because the phrase is a fixed one (Isaiah 13:19; Jeremiah 50:40). The text does not say what disaster struck part of Israel in this way; it may have been war, or an earthquake like the one in 1:1.

decisions.choice: a stick snatched from the burning: barely saved, already scorched
decisions.reason: A stick pulled out of the fire is saved, but only just, and it is charred (Zechariah 3:2). Israel had survived, but narrowly, and still it did not return.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: some (L in brackets, B, R); as completely as; the rest of you; just in time (R)
decisions.reason: "Among you" means that part of the people was struck, and every level supplies "some". Readable says what the comparisons mean (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: um tição
decisions.reason: "Tição", a piece of wood already burning, is the exact Portuguese word for the picture (m2); Readable describes it.

source.text: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֵ֚קֶב כִּֽי־זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הִכּ֥וֹן לִקְרַאת־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus I will do to you, Israel; because this I will do to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.

en.L: Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; \q because this I will do to you, \q prepare to meet your God, O Israel!
en.B: So this is what I will do to you, Israel; \q and because I am going to do this to you, \q prepare to meet your God, Israel!
en.R: So, Israel, this is what I will do to you. \q And because I am going to do this to you, \q get ready to meet your God, Israel!

pt.L: Por isso assim farei a vocês, ó Israel; \q porque isto farei a vocês, \q preparem-se para encontrar o seu Deus, ó Israel!
pt.B: Por isso é assim que vou fazer com vocês, Israel; \q e, porque vou fazer isto com vocês, \q preparem-se para encontrar o seu Deus, Israel!
pt.R: Por isso, Israel, é isto que vou fazer com vocês. \q E, porque vou fazer isto com vocês, \q preparem-se para encontrar o seu Deus, Israel!

decisions.choice: thus I will do to you: what the LORD will do is not said
decisions.reason: "Thus" and "this" usually point to something said next, but nothing follows. The LORD leaves the threat open, which makes it more fearful than any description. Some take "this" to point back to the judgments already announced (3:11-15; 4:2-3), others forward to the meeting with God in the same verse.

decisions.choice: prepare to meet your God: the words of Sinai, now a summons to judgment
decisions.reason: At Sinai the people were told to "be ready", and Moses brought them out "to meet God" (Exodus 19:11, 15, 17). Israel will meet its God again, but after five refusals to return (verses 6-11) the meeting will be for judgment. Some hear in the words a last call to repent before that meeting, but the verse itself announces it.

decisions.choice: O Israel (L), Israel (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal marks the calling out of Israel's name with "O", as in Hosea; Balanced and Readable use the name alone. Readable says "get ready" for "prepare".

decisions.choice: Preparem-se para encontrar o seu Deus (vocês)
alternatives: Prepara-te para encontrar o teu Deus (tu)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here, Israel called by name as one, and Portuguese could say "tu". It keeps "vocês", the address of verses 4-11 to the same people, so that the summons does not seem to turn to someone new, and so that the line reads as a call to every hearer. The words recall Sinai, where the people prepared to meet God (m2).

source.text: כִּ֡י הִנֵּה֩ יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ עֹשֵׂ֥ה שַׁ֨חַר֙ עֵיפָ֔ה וְדֹרֵ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי אָ֑רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, [the one] forming mountains and creating wind, and declaring to humankind what [is] his thought, making dawn darkness, and treading on [the] heights of [the] earth: Yahweh, God of hosts, [is] his name.

en.L: For look, the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to humankind what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thought [is], \q who makes the dawn darkness, \q and treads on the earth's heights: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thoughts to humankind, \q who turns the dawn into darkness \q and treads on the heights of the earth: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: He formed the mountains and created the wind. He tells people what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is planning. \q He turns the dawn into darkness \q and walks on the high places of the earth. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies.

pt.L: Pois eis que aquele que forma os montes e cria o vento, e declara ao ser humano qual [é] o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} pensamento, \q que faz da aurora escuridão, \q e pisa sobre as alturas da terra: \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, [é] o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.
pt.B: Pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é quem forma os montes e cria o vento, quem revela à humanidade os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pensamentos, \q quem transforma a aurora em escuridão \q e pisa sobre as alturas da terra: \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.
pt.R: Ele formou os montes e criou o vento. Ele conta às pessoas o que está planejando. \q Ele transforma a manhã em escuridão \q e anda sobre os lugares altos da terra. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome.

decisions.choice: a hymn to the Creator: the God whom Israel must meet
decisions.reason: The verse is a short hymn: a string of descriptions of God ("who forms ... who creates ... who treads") closing with "the LORD God of hosts is his name". Similar hymns stand in 5:8-9 and 9:5-6. It answers verse 12: the God Israel must prepare to meet is the maker of mountains and wind, who rules the whole earth.

decisions.choice: wind: the wind, created by God
decisions.reason: The word can mean wind, breath or spirit. Beside "mountains" it means the wind, part of the created world (Psalm 135:7; Jeremiah 10:13).

decisions.choice: declares to humankind what his thought is: God makes his own purpose known
alternatives: he shows a person his own thoughts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "what his thought is", and "his" could be God or the person. Most likely God makes his own plans known to people, as he reveals his secret to the prophets (3:7). It can also mean that God shows a person his own hidden thoughts (Psalm 139:2; Jeremiah 11:20).

decisions.choice: who makes the dawn darkness: he turns morning into darkness
alternatives: who makes the dawn and the darkness
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and". They can mean that God turns dawn into darkness, as in the judgment of 5:8 and 8:9, or that he makes both dawn and darkness, the order of day and night.

decisions.choice: treads on the heights of the earth: the LORD strides over the world as its ruler
decisions.reason: Micah 1:3 uses the same words of the LORD coming down in judgment; Deuteronomy 32:13 and Job 9:8 speak of treading on the heights in the same way. To tread on a place is to rule it.

decisions.choice: the LORD God of hosts (L), the LORD God of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: Where Amos joins "God of hosts" directly to the divine name, the wording is "the LORD God of hosts" at Literal and "the LORD God of Armies" at Balanced and Readable, as in the Psalms (Psalm 80:5; 84:9) and in Amos 5:14-16, 27; 6:8, 14. On the title, see 3:13. Balanced and Readable turn the descriptions into clauses about God ("he is the one who", "He formed"), and Readable puts his name at the end in its own sentence.

decisions.choice: O SENHOR, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o seu nome ([é] at Literal)
alternatives: O seu nome é SENHOR Deus dos Exércitos
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the close of the three hymns (4:13; 5:8-9; 9:5-6) keeps one wording at every level, with the Hebrew order, the name first: "O SENHOR, o Deus dos Exércitos, é o seu nome", and "O SENHOR é o seu nome" where the Hebrew has the divine name alone (5:8; 9:6). Readable keeps it too, so that the refrain is heard as one, rather than the English Readable's "His name is". "O Deus dos Exércitos" as at 3:13.

decisions.choice: ao ser humano
decisions.reason: The word means humankind (m3); "o ser humano" says it without a gender setting, which the English does not use here either.
